tips.comment: This one also has an entry at Newbury on Friday but this looks an easier assignment so I feel this is the one Hughes will choose to run in. If so it will be a tip in itself

Comes from top trainer Willie Mullins and has found itself in a smaller, weaker field of runners. Came second on seasonal debut, 7 lengths behind the leader, so probably needed the run out. Steps up in trip by 4 furlongs, and the jockey gets a 7-pound claimer, both of which are bonuses for the horse. Looks to be a consistent type, and improvement is likely. Should get off the mark today.

Horse that likes being stepped up in trip after finishing 2nd at Ballinrobe over 16.5f won well at Wexford over 21f by 4L 11 days ago . Steps up an extra 1f again today but J.Kennedy is out the plate & 7Lb claimer takes the ride , slight worry about 11 day turnaround .

Western Ability is a six-year-old gelding trained by D M Christie and ridden by B W Harvey. He was beaten just over 8 lengths over 3m2f at Sligo last time but stuck on steadily and ran better than the bare result. Placed in both runs over this course and distance and one of three runs at this venue, he seems to enjoy this sort of stamina test. Has cheekpieces go back on and may now be much fitter after two runs back. Although still a maiden, he has shown me enough to suggest he could pop up at a price, especially if they go hard early and it turns into a slog, as his running style will be held up behind a decent pace and could plug on late if others falter in this wide-open looking race here.
Won well on hurdles debut in May. Disappointing on next run, but ground didn't suit. Gets good ground today and upped in trip, which should be a plus.
Fitness is taken on trust but is not normally an issue for a Willie Mullins newcomer. I don’t think he would have named one Closutton unless it was useful, so it can make a winning start.

Closutton is very nicely bred and could be useful for the Willie Mullins stable but backing a horse at odds on first time out when there are promising alternatives looks a risk and the comments in the Racing Post from the stable were that she was decent but not a world beater. Walks The Talk looks to have a decent chance to upset the odds. She bolted up in a point to point at Dromahane and ran a nice first race under rules behind a very good horse. She may have needed that a bit as it was her first run since October and John McConnell has a very good record in bumpers, so she looks to have a good each way chance. She is also very nicely bred and open to plenty of improvement.

Did not run that badly on debut run, as they were hampered 4f out and then stayed on well final 2f to come 6/12 beaten 16.5 lengths in a similar level NHF race over 2.1 miles @ Bellestown. Entitled to come on for that run/experience, step up to this 2.3 miles should suit and in hands of a shrewd trainer, making current 20/1 decent Ew value in the race.

Elana Osario is a 4-year-old filly trained by P Twomey. She finally got her head in front on her penultimate start, having shown a lot of early promise. She stepped up in trip latest and posted a career-high RPR of 87 when just failing to get up to the progressive filly Heather and lost by a head on her handicap debut - clear of the rest by some 4.5l. There should be more to come, being a sixth foal and a full sister to five individual winners, three of which posted RPRs of 109, 109, and 117, and out of a Listed winning dam who won on good to soft (yielding today, which is essentially good to soft). Colin Keane rides, and his filly also brings course form to the table, finishing runner-up to an A P O'Brien trained Get (77) by 2.25 lengths on heavy ground over CD. Get is now rated 100, and she won't be inconvenienced by any further rain. The welterweight of 10 stone is the only issue, but she must have a big chance.on form and pedigree.
A maiden winner in May and two good runs since. 3/7 last time out when up in trip as BF, badly hampered that day and can do better. Regular jockey GM Ryan back on board.

Clearly goes well with cut in the ground as they showed again Lto, when coming 2/15 beaten 4.5 lengths in a slightly lesser handicap over 1.1 miles @ Leopardstown. That was only their 4th run so clearly should have a lot of improvement in them, only 1lb higher here, pieces on first time, good jockey up (D McMonagle prefers stable favourite in the race) and top trainer best here numerically last 5 seasons, making current 14/1 solid Ew value in the race.

You can make a case for a fair few of these but at the odds ex-French trained Raybiya looks the value bet. French form was decent and made an encouraging debut for new connections when 5th over an inadequate trip at Roscommon.

Step up in trip seemed to work wonders. Overcame trouble in running to do so. Goes further in trip again, but the way he finished his last race, there's no reason to see why this test in stamina won't bring out the best again.

Mon St Michel has been aimed at this race since the start of the year with Pat Smullen's teenage son riding, Paddy Smullen. The track will be alight for this race. They want to see the deceased jockey's son come home with his first winner. If he does, 'the roof comes off the stand' with the noise! A very well-bred horse can win this comfortably and land our NAP. After all, this horse was four lengths behind Kyprios in the Levmoss Stakes at Leopardstown two months ago!

ROYAL HOLLOW has been placed in two races from four starts also won two hurdle races at 2m 1f second over 1m 7f at Leopardstown on her latest outing last month dropped in trip to 1m 6f should suit and could well be able to go one better and win this race

Slightly intriguing runner for Charles Byrnes who has trained a decent stayer in the past (Run For Oscar). 40-1 winner of a handicap hurdle over 2 miles at Limerick in October, otherwise very little form to note. Some staying potential in pedigree on the dam's side. Only five years old, with Clive Cox as a youngster, placed twice. Interesting in that he ran five days ago and could potentially come on for that outing. 7lbs claimer Glen Norris retains the ride.
Has won her last two races and has already beaten five of today's rivals previously. Should make a bold bid for the hat-trick.

Jasmine Affanalis is a 3-year-old filly trained by David Marnane and ridden by Luke McAteer. She was raised 2lb by the Irish handicapper from 53-55 for a promising 2/15 at Limerick on her penultimate start when going down by 3 lengths to In The Minus (52 received 1lb), a horse that has subsequently finished a neck runner-up in a claimer, posting a career-high RPR of 68. Jasmine Affanalis was slightly disappointing on her last start, but there were excuses: 'Midfield, switched right and ran on from 2f out, hampered on inner inside final furlong, kept on (jockey said filly was hampered a furlong down).' Luke and David generally make a formidable combination in handicaps on runners who are sent off at 10-1 or less, with 28/90 wins showing a healthy LSP of £97.12. If Jasmine Affanalis avoids trouble, she could be very well handicapped given the form she showed on her penultimate start at Limerick. Chance!

We are getting 3 places here. After returning from a 5-month break, it came 4th at Ayr in a 7f classified race. Did all the best work at the finish and looked like this extra furlong will benefit today. But also came from a long way back that day and will want to be closer today. Already has a featherweight of 8-8 and has another 7lb off with this claimer as well. There is all but 2 stone between this and 2nd fav Oiche Rua.

Finished in the frame on 7 of 10 outings for previous stable. Got no run from a poor draw on debut for this yard at the Curragh last time. Now down a pound and top rider on board, should be tough to beat.

Not too sure she enjoyed the soft going last time out, and it was also her first run of the season. It doesn't look like a great race, to be honest, with the favorite having its first run for a year, and the second favorite didn't look much last time out. But we have two runners having their first race as well and could be anything. Sister Lily did improve from last year's run, and with fitness and better ground, she should improve again.
Failed to impress on chase debut last time. Reverts back to hurdles. Won over course and distance here on penultimate start and is 5lb higher here. Chance as he won easy enough on that last win.

Noel Kelly's mare showed her first piece of worthwhile form over CD in May and then possibly surpassed that when finishing just over 6 lengths behind her well-gambled stablemate Nakassama at Hexham 38 days ago over 2 furlongs shorter. She was unfancied on both occasions and was probably there as a companion on her Northumberland jaunt. I don't think she'll be unfancied here over her right trip and 6 pounds lower than last time.

Taking a bit of a punter's calculated gamble here. Intersky Sunset is an 8-year-old mare trained by D Queally and ridden by J P O'Sullivan. She has yet to win from 12 starts in handicap company but has placed four times, including once over this distance. Last time out, she finished beaten over 3m at Tipperary, finding little up in trip and on quicker ground. I am judging her on the earlier form when placing in more moderately run races, and the return to a stiffer test of stamina could help if they go a good pace. She tends to be held up, so a strongly run contest would suit, especially if the leaders overdo it. Her running positioning will depend on how the race unfolds early on, but she usually will likely be held up again. Needs to bounce back, but if ground eases and others fade late, she could sneak in here.
They are stepping this one back up in trip slightly with a 7 lbs claiming jockey booking/change. A good value each way bet for the 4 places available.

Sights Unseen is up 5lb for her last win over hurdles and that may be a bit too much so an each way dabble on Sir Carnegie is suggested. He has shown ability but can be clumsy over the obstacles. However he did complete over this C&D in May (5th of 9) and any improvement on that would see him in the mix.

Shark Hanlon's 7 year old French Gelding FIREWORKS has gotten under my skin more than he should have & now I can't shake the fact I think he may have a small each way chance here. This Son of KINGSMAN ran as well as to be expected at Wexford 48 days ago when coming off a mammoth 517 day sabbatical yes he jumped a bit rusty (which was to be expected) but I thought he ran ok & was making a bit of headway 3 from the lollypop before tiring & prior to this there was another run off a break (albeit not as significant) so I'm keen to see how this French Charge fares now (hopefully) rust free. This lad has dropped another 2lbs and gets the services of in form 5lb claimer Shane O'Callaghan who has a very impressive 75% place strike rate this past month. Trainer has a 35.29% place strike rate here in Northern Ireland the past year. Certainly not one to put the mortgage on but the curiosity has me & at 22/1 I'll allow it.

Yes, the form line is far from inspiring and deserves to be at long odds. But sometimes a change of scenery can work the oracle for a horse who has been found wanting in a bigger yard. Rosemary Connors now has this mare, and this is her first run for Rosie. Looked useful at Thurles a season back on debut over bigger fences. In her only run over them this time, she was prominent but then found wanting and wasn't persevered with. A repeat of that effort at Thurles could bring her into contention.

Fool Me Once has shown steady progression, with a strong 2nd (beaten 4½l) over 2m 6f at this course in his latest outing. His 0% win rate but 28.57% place rate in hurdle races (2 placings from 7 starts) and suitability for a stiff test make him a strong contender.

Ollie La Ba Ba is a 7-year-old gelding trained by E McCarthy and partnered by G B Noonan, claiming 5lb. He has had 32 runs with a win rate of 6% and a place rate of 19%. He has a strong course profile with 1 win and 1 place from 2 starts at Downpatrick and loves this sound surface. He fell last time in a beginners' chase at Roscommon when still in the mix of things. That came after a solid hurdles season where he ran to a fair level in handicaps. Currently on a doable mark and now back at a track that he loves. If ridden prominently again, he could win here as the tongue strap and cheekpieces combination has produced previous success
Divilabother is still looking for its first win after thirteen outings, but this looks to be a perfect opportunity after finishing second last time.
Fit from the flat this one has shown a modicum in a handful of hurdle races and represents a yard in excellent form so given an each way squeak in an open race.
Won on the flat last time off a mark of 65. Last run over jumps off 94 in May when placed and is allowed in here off the same mark. Very much well in on flat mark. Decent chance.

Ar Nos Na Gaoithe was pulled from a race yesterday so strong signs that trainer has decided to run him today. Has been racing consistently well and should feature if running to same level. Strong traveller who went close here last time out. NAP
Point winner who ran her best race under rules to date at Perth last time out and looks quite well treated on this handicap debut.

Portarlington has slipped to an attractive mark after winning three on the bounce last year. Ran a better race last time out at Roscommon. The jockey won two of those three wins and has a recent win to his name with a win at Bellewstown. This doesn't look like a strong race and is there for the taking.
Order Of The Dance would probably have finished further up the field had it not been hampered in its last race. It had two seconds previously.

Tyson is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Paul Nolan and ridden by Ben Stone, who claims 7lb. He returns from a break and wears cheekpieces for the very first time. These could sharpen him up here. Placed in 2 of 5 starts on similar ground and once in 4 attempts off this mark. Was down the field last time over 2 miles at Wexford, but may improve with that last run and the headgear today. Not one to rule out if the race sets up to suit and he bounces back today as he will be ridden patiently from midfield and If they go hard up front, he could sneak into the race late.
Chance taking on the horse that ran well last time out in a Class 5. Went off big odds then, stepping up in class but 5 pounds better off than last race.

Annie Agnew is a 5-year-old gelding trained by Gerald Stephen Quinn and remains unexposed in handicaps having only had four starts. She makes a reappearance after a 332- day absence off a career-low handicap mark of 102. There are a couple of reasons why that won't matter. Firstly, the trainer sent three horses to Perth on the 13th of July, and they finished 2-1-1, so clearly his yard is in good nick. Secondly, Annie Agnew goes well fresh. She finished 2/12 on debut at Ballinrobe at 40-1, then won a maiden hurdle on the next start, beating Spinning Web and Doctor Nightingale, who have both won since and have been rated 125-113. So Annie Agnew could be chucked in off 102 if we presume She's fit and ready. He then had a 303-day break and performed well at Perth, finishing 2/8, and was subsequently raised to 108. He can go well fresh, and I hope the yard's good form reflects in today's performance after a lengthy absence.

His two runs this year suggest he has improved for a winter break, and he may be ready to shed his maiden tag today. His fourth place finish in a Sligo claimer last month probably constituted a career best, and a reproduction of that form now returned to handicap company off a career low mark might just be good enough.

Enchanted Garden has won 3 of her 9 starts the last coming at Leopardstown off a mark of 72 in April. She has been unplaced since off 77 at Curragh in May and 74 last month but now down to 73 with Jack Cleary taking off 5lbs she looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer

Harry The Rogue is a 4-year-old gelding trained by Andrew Slattery. He has won over 1m here and at Naas this year and continues in fine form year-to-date, rising from a mark of 50 (Naas win) to a current mark of 72. He is both consistent and progressive. He posted a career-high RPR of 74 last time out off 67 and has been raised a further 5lb when beaten by a head, finishing 2/16 by another progressive sort in Finsceal Annie over 7f, at Leopardstown one of Irelands flagship tracks a horse who had previously won over CD. The winner opened on a mark of 50 and now rated 78, a 28lb improvement from the 4- year-old filly. Todays step back up to a mile seems the right move and Sam Coen knows this fella well having won on him at Killarney and Naas amSlattery remaina in good form (7/33) with his My Girl Sioux battling gamely to fend off challenge after challenge at Navan to make to land a second win in a row just yesterday.
Has been very consistent and did well to finish fourth of fifteen at Leopardstown last time out after missing the break. Can make amends here with more luck at the start.
Goldrush Kid showed promise with a recent fourth in a tougher handicap. Dropping in grade here, he's well-placed for a strong performance. The anticipated rain should also be in his favour.

I feel there is a plot brewing here for Tony Martin's French 5 year old Gelding ZUZUKEL & to my untrained eye she was held back a little when last seen on the turf. This Son of the Mighty FRANKEL was plodding on fair enough through the juice filled turf at Limerick(1f Soft) on penultimate with 2nd,3rd & 4th placed going on to win since. Obviously the fact that Top jockey Colin Keane remains in the plate is a big plus & certainly shows this yards intentions. Trainer has a 46.67% place strike this past month. Back to the turf for handicap debut here with the underfoot sludge from a pedigree point of view should work in his favour. I could be wrong (and quite possibly am) but I think this charge will be let of the leesh a bit sooner (if they even adopt hold up tactics that is) I'm happy to be wrong & at 14/1 currently ill side with this French Lad each way.

Purring Along was harshly demoted to 2nd in my opinion on the last run. Travelled smoothly and finished with a rattle. Has been able to front run in the past, so tactically versatile and should give a good run despite the 7lb penalty.

Experienced gelding. Won for this jockey back in May. A bit disappointing since though did OK over an inadequate trip last time out and can't be ruled out back over a mile and with underfoot conditions to suit.

A winner off 62 and a 2nd off 67 over this CD, races off 63 today and has the assistance of an in-form 10lb claimer on board. The horse looks to be coming back into form again after leading and fading in the final furlong last time out. Worth an E/W put at 18/1 with 4 places on offer.

BRAINS wins when he likes and is difficult to predict when it’s his going day, but there’s a few factors here to suggest he might go close today .. he’s a 13 times distance winner so no issues with the trip, the going has come up soft here overnight and he’s a winner and placed on it and he’s back down to just 1lb above his last winning mark.. the draw isn’t ideal in 12 and he’s a 9 y/o so he’s vulnerable.. but he could easily outrun these odds..

He's a big outsider and understandably so given that his form took a downward turn in the second half of last year. His first two runs of 2024 were quite promising however, a fourth over today's course and distance then finishing third at Fairyhouse sixteen days later. He may be best caught fresh on that limited evidence, and he's eight pounds lower today. Highly speculative but potentially very rewarding at huge odds.

Zanahiyr is taken to score for Gordon Elliott (SR 20%). Ran fourth behind stablemate Mordor over course and distance on last run back in May. Likely better for a break of 63 days since then and any rain will be a positive for his chances. Grade 2 winning hurdler in the past. Reliable, talented stayer dropped 1 pound in the handicap and looks decently handicapped here on a mark of 76 (9 stone 5 pounds). 8yo by Nathaniel. Declan McDonogh up again.
One old-timer I regularly put up but also gets regularly withdrawn is Lord Erskine, which if goes, could put this lot away if on that good day. Nibbles for it already.

He's a well-bred Dubawi gelding who has shown ability over this distance and mark, previously winning on the Flat and twice over the hurdles. He looks a stayer in the making, while the stable booking looks positive. On balance, the best on form in this field.

I fancy this horse will make the frame in this race. Last time out, it ran a very eye-catching run. It ran on from the back in a Curragh 2-mile handicap that suited the front runners, and this horse was the only one making ground on the placed horses. Today, it gets its ground and is 2lb lower than its last winning mark.
There are a few with good chances in this race and I am going to side with Lady Pagasa who has placed in the last 4 races and will be fresh from a lay off.

Piatra Neamt is lightly raced, showing promise on debut, and steps up in trip, which looks likely to suit based on pedigree and the trainer's comment saying they needed a longer distance. SM Duffy doesn't carry a flashy record, but this could be a sharp placement in a weak field where most rivals are thoroughly exposed. Yielding to soft ground on this distance should help a late-running type like this settle.
